title: From Belief Inference to Task Action: A Multi-Level Evaluation of Theory of Mind on Verifiable Tasks
abstract: arXiv:2610.34759v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Effective collaboration requires language models to understand what others know and believe, and to act accordingly. Models that assume others share their information may omit necessary communication and undermine coordination. Many theory-of-mind (ToM) benchmarks assess mental-state inference through story questions, but correct answers do not establish that models can use these judgments in subsequent tasks. We introduce a multi-level evaluation built on existing, verifiable tasks. We extend household collaboration and calendar scheduling with asymmetric information while retaining their original constraints and validators. Independent interfaces assess world understanding, information access, beliefs, decisions, and execution. Controls supply personal evidence or correct beliefs to distinguish state recovery from state use. Across six model configurations, these abilities diverge. translated_title: 从信念推断到任务行动：在可验证任务上对心智理论的多层次评估
translated_abstract: 有效的协作要求语言模型理解他人知道什么、相信什么，并据此采取行动。那些假设他人拥有与自己相同信息的模型可能会省略必要的沟通，从而破坏协调配合。许多心智理论基准通过故事问答来评估心理状态推断能力，但正确回答这些问题并不能证明模型能够在后续任务中运用这些判断。我们提出了一种建立在现有可验证任务之上的多层次评估方法。我们在保留原有约束条件和验证器的前提下，将家庭协作与日历安排任务扩展为具有非对称信息的场景。通过相互独立的接口，分别评估对世界的理解、信息获取、信念、决策和执行能力。对照组通过提供个人证据或正确信念，来区分“恢复他人状态”与“运用他人状态”这两种能力。在六种模型配置中，这些能力表现出明显的分化。在匹配的日程安排案例中，Claude 恢复了所有智能体的……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该研究提出了一个基于可验证任务的多层次心智理论评估框架，将家庭协作与日历安排任务扩展为非对称信息场景，用以区分语言模型“推断他人信念”与“将信念运用于实际协作行动”这两种能力的差异。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces a multi-level theory-of-mind evaluation built on verifiable tasks with asymmetric information, revealing a divergence between language models' ability to infer others' beliefs and their ability to act on those beliefs in collaborative tasks.
